Resolve a "ties_*" rounding string

Source: R/resolve-ties-rounding.R
resolve_ties_rounding.Rd

resolve_ties_rounding() translates one of the "ties_*" rounding strings into the rounding and symmetric values it stands for, such as "ties_away" into rounding = "up" and symmetric = TRUE. Any other rounding is returned unchanged, along with symmetric.

reround() and unround() resolve these strings the same way, so a function that branches on rounding itself can call this first to agree with them.

Usage

resolve_ties_rounding(rounding, symmetric)

Arguments

rounding

String (length 1). A rounding method. Not checked.

symmetric

Logical (length 1). See round_up(). Not checked.

Value

A list with the elements rounding and symmetric.

Details

resolve_ties_rounding() is a low-level primitive and does not check its input. The caller is responsible for passing a single string as rounding and a single TRUE or FALSE as symmetric. In particular, a number as rounding would pick a "ties_*" method by position.

Combining a "ties_*" string with symmetric = TRUE is an error, because the string already determines how negative ties are broken.

Examples

resolve_ties_rounding("ties_away", symmetric = FALSE)
#> $rounding
#> [1] "up"
#> 
#> $symmetric
#> [1] TRUE
#> 

# Other methods pass through:
resolve_ties_rounding("up", symmetric = TRUE)
#> $rounding
#> [1] "up"
#> 
#> $symmetric
#> [1] TRUE
#>
